title: How to Make a TikTok Ad for Your Store | AIVideosUGC
description: Learn how to make a TikTok ad from a single product photo: plan the opening, make a vertical video, add captions and music in TikTok, then launch. Start here.
h1: How to Make a TikTok Ad When You've Never Made One
lead: Learn how to make a TikTok ad for one product: choose a clear reason to buy, plan the opening, then review each publishing step.
summary: Plan, make, and launch a simple vertical TikTok ad for one product, starting from a single photo.

sections.h2: Pick one product and one reason to buy
paras: First ads often try to say too much. Choose one product and finish this sentence: "People buy this because..." Keep the answer short and specific.

"A phone stand that folds flat enough to slip into a jacket pocket" is a strong reason. "High quality, versatile, and stylish" isn't, because there's nothing to show. That specific answer gives you a clear scene to plan.

A few more examples: a candle that burns evenly to the bottom of the jar, a dog leash with a clip you can open with one hand, a lunch box with a lid that doesn't leak when tipped. Each one points to a scene you can picture.
People scroll [TikTok](page:plat-tiktok) fast. If the opening doesn't give them something to watch, they're gone before your product appears. Skip logo intros and slow fades.

Openings that hold attention show the product doing something right away: a hand snapping the phone stand open, [a drink poured over ice](page:tpl-drink), a sneaker turning to show its sole. Pick one moment that matches your reason to buy.

sections.h2: Make the video from your product photo
paras: In [AIVideosUGC Video Ads](page:video-ads), upload a clear photo of the product and write one sentence describing the scene, such as "A hand unfolds a slim black phone stand on a cafe table and sets a phone in it, soft daylight." Choose 9:16, the full-screen vertical shape TikTok uses. The [ad sizes guide](page:guide-ad-sizes-by-platform) explains the other shapes. A [lifestyle product photo](page:lifestyle-photos) can give the same campaign a still image for the feed.

Then pick a length. Six seconds suits a single moment, like the stand snapping open. Ten seconds leaves room for a short demo. Fifteen seconds fits a simple sequence: unfold, place the phone, start a video call. Thirty seconds leaves room for a longer sequence. The credit cost appears before the video starts.

Each run makes one video. To try a second opening, run it again with a changed sentence. Keep the request about the scene and leave prices and headlines out. You'll add those next, where you control every letter.

sections.h2: Add text, captions, and sound in TikTok or CapCut
paras: Open the video in TikTok's editor or CapCut. Add one short line near the start that names the benefit, like "Folds flat. Fits your pocket." Then add the price or offer if you have one.
Keep all text in the middle of the screen. TikTok places the account name, the caption, and the like and share buttons along the bottom and right edge, and they cover anything underneath.
Add sound in the same editor. For ads, pick from TikTok's Commercial Music Library or another source licensed for business use, since many songs people use in regular posts aren't cleared for ads.

sections.h2: Run a quick check before launch
paras: Check that the product and main text still make sense with the sound off, then confirm the soundtrack is clear with the sound on.

Then ask a few plain questions. Is the product on screen within the first second? Can you read every word without pausing? Do the color and version in the video match what the product page sells? Is the price in the ad the same as the price at checkout?
If any answer is no, fix it now. A mismatch between the ad and the product page is one of the fastest ways to waste a click you paid for.

sections.h2: Launch small and watch what happens
paras: In TikTok Ads Manager, create a campaign with a goal that matches what you want, such as traffic to your store or sales. Set a daily budget you're comfortable spending while you learn, send viewers to the product page for the item in the video, and add a clear button like "Shop now."
Write the ad caption the way you'd text a friend about the product: one line, plain words, no wall of hashtags. For the phone stand, "Fits in your pocket, holds your phone at eye level" says enough.

Let it run for a few days before you judge it. Look at how many people watch past the first few seconds, how many click, and what each sale costs. If you made a second opening, compare both in the same group of ads and see which one people stay with. The [guide to testing ad versions](page:guide-testing-ad-versions) shows how to compare them fairly.

checklist: One product and one specific reason to buy
An opening that shows the product in action
Text and price added in TikTok or CapCut, away from the edges
A small budget and a few days before you decide

faq.q: How can I compare two TikTok openings?
faq.a: Make two versions with the same product, offer, and destination. Change only the opening, then compare the results in Ads Manager.

faq.q: Do I need to label an AI-made video on TikTok?
faq.a: Yes. TikTok asks advertisers to label realistic AI-generated content, and Ads Manager includes a setting for it when you create the ad. Policies change, so read [TikTok's current ad policies](https://ads.tiktok.com/help/article/about-ad-disclaimers-in-tiktok-ads-manager?lang=en) before you launch.

faq.q: What should I add after downloading the TikTok ad?
faq.a: Add captions, licensed sound, price, and call to action in TikTok or CapCut. Upload the finished 9:16 file in TikTok Ads Manager.
